subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the 3×3 matrix with 3 on every diagonal entry and 0 elsewhere, then find A⁴.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.100 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 147. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Recognise A as 3I
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the whole question. A is 3 times the identity, so powers of A are powers of 3 times the identity — no matrix multiplication needed at all.
steps.memory_tip: A is 3 times the identity, so powers of A are powers of 3 times I — no matrix multiplication needed.

recall.must_convey: That A is recognised as 3I, a scalar multiple of the identity.
accept: A is three times the identity matrix
recognise it as three I so powers are easy
take the three out as a scalar
it is a scalar multiple of the identity

steps.why: Spotting the scalar multiple turns four matrix multiplications into one arithmetic step. Multiplying it out four times gives the same answer far more slowly.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the matrix by itself four times.

steps.label: Raise to the fourth power
steps.margin_note: Second mark. (3I)⁴ = 3⁴I⁴, and I to any power is I — so the answer is 81I.
steps.memory_tip: (3I)⁴ = 3⁴I⁴, and I to any power is I, so the answer is 81I.

lines.text: A⁴ = 81I, that is 81 on the diagonal and 0 elsewhere

accept: three I to the fourth is eighty one times I to the fourth which is eighty one I
three to the fourth is eighty one and I stays I
the answer is eighty one I
three power four eighty one, I power four I, so eighty one I
A to the fourth is eighty one I

steps.why: The identity is unchanged by any power, which is exactly what makes it the multiplicative identity. Only the scalar does any work.
common_mistakes: Putting 81 in every entry rather than only the diagonal.
